page: Amazon Web Services i3.2xlarge is an x86_64 storage-optimized instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The system includes 61.0 GB of memory (7.62 GB per vCPU) and a 45 MB L3 cache. It features a bundled local storage capacity of 1900 GB on NVMe SSD, 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not include hardware accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate that the older Broadwell-era processor exhibits limited raw compute capability. Both single-core and multi-core evaluations—including stress-ng and Geekbench—rate within the bottom 10% to 25% of modern cloud instance profiles. The passmark CPU score registers at 6204.12, reflecting reduced throughput in compute-heavy tasks such as compilation and cryptographic processing. The processor supports AVX and AES instructions but lacks newer vector expansions like AVX-512.

Memory and operational benchmarks present mid-tier to lower-range results. Large-block read bandwidth attains 41.72 GB/sec, placing it in the middle tier, whereas cached small-block reads and uncached write bandwidth fall into the lower quartiles. In real-world service simulations, Redis SET operations achieve 2.37 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 5.19 GB/sec. LLM text generation rates also remain constrained, achieving 89.88 tokens/sec on a small 135M model and dropping to 5.24 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

Resource allocation on the i3.2xlarge is heavily balanced toward dense, high-capacity NVMe storage rather than pure processor throughput. As a result, its qualitative cost efficiency is defined by its integrated fast local disk footprint per vCPU rather than compute density. Workloads best suited for this instance include distributed file systems, NoSQL databases, log analysis nodes, and data store caching layers where fast local NVMe read/write access takes precedence over compute-bound processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i3.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 4-core, 8-vCPU Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. Configured on an x86_64 architecture with the Xen hypervisor, it provides 61.0 GB of RAM alongside 1900 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network profile. It contains no GPUs. Benchmark metrics reveal lower-percentile compute performance, with Geekbench and stress-ng scores reflecting older CPU architecture constraints, though memory performance remains mid-tier during large uncached reads (41.72 GB/sec). With substantial local NVMe storage and balanced memory, the i3.2xlarge delivers a qualitative cost advantage for storage-dense configurations rather than pure processing power. It is well-fitted for storage-intensive applications, operational NoSQL engines, distributed caching nodes, and transactional databases that rely directly on low-latency local disk I/O.
